title: $g$-wave altermagnetic order parameter in hematite
authors: Tianren Wang, Yuehong Li, Yu Feng, Andong Liu, Yuetong Wu, Qian Zhao, Yujie Yan, Wei Luo, Xin Tong, Yi Lu, Yao Shen, Stefano Agrestini, Jaewon Choi, Qisi Wang
abstract: Altermagnets combine the vanishing net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Magnon band splitting provides a direct probe of altermagnetic order and may enable chirality-selective magnon transport, yet the momentum-space symmetry of this splitting has not been determined quantitatively. Here we use inelastic neutron scattering to map the momentum dependence of altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite ($α$-Fe$_2$O$_3$). The splitting vanishes along nodal directions and reaches maxima off the nodes, revealing the $g$-wave symmetry of the altermagnetic order parameter. These results agree with linear spin-wave theory calculations based on the altermagnetic model, which further identify the nondegenerate branches as magnons of opposite chirality and trace the splitting to symmetry-inequivalent long-range exchange interactions. Our results provide the first quantitative determination of the momentum-space symmetry of altermagnetic chiral magnons. These findings, together with hematite's high magnetic ordering temperature and low magnon damping, establish it as a promising platform for low-dissipation, symmetry-selective magnonic applications.
summary: This work uses inelastic neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to determine the symmetry of the magnetic order in hematite. By measuring the momentum-dependent splitting of magnons, the authors conclusively establish a $g$-wave symmetry for the altermagnetic order parameter. This finding positions hematite as a promising platform for advanced, symmetry-selective magnonic applications.
main_problem: To quantitatively determine the momentum-space symmetry of the altermagnetic order parameter in hematite ($\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$).
main_result: The magnon splitting exhibits a $g$-wave symmetry, vanishing along nodal directions and maximizing off the nodes, confirming the altermagnetic nature of the order parameter.
method: The study combines inelastic neutron scattering (INS) measurements with Linear Spin-Wave Theory (LSWT) calculations.
model_or_system: The system is hematite ($\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$), an altermagnet, modeled using an effective Heisenberg Hamiltonian that incorporates an asymmetry ($\Delta$) between two symmetry-inequivalent long-range exchange paths ($J^{(1)}_{13}$ and $J^{(2)}_{13}$).
key_observables: Altermagnetic magnon splitting, $\Delta(Q) = |E_{\uparrow}(Q) - E_{\downarrow}(Q)|$, and the chiral response $S_{+-}(Q, \omega) - S_{-+}(Q, \omega)$.
important_parameters: The splitting magnitude ($\approx 100$ meV) and the momentum dependence ($\Delta(	heta)$) are key diagnostic tools.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed splitting is dominated by the asymmetry between the two long-range exchange interactions, and that the magnon splitting can be mapped to the order parameter symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exchange network, the momentum dependence of the splitting (showing nodal vs. off-nodal behavior), and comparisons between experimental INS data and LSWT calculations for both altermagnetic and conventional AFM models.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, presents the theoretical model incorporating symmetry-breaking exchange terms, details the experimental INS measurements, and validates the $g$-wave symmetry by comparing the measured angular dependence against LSWT predictions.
why_interesting: The precise mapping of magnetic order parameter symmetry via magnon spectroscopy is a powerful tool for understanding complex magnetic ground states, which has implications for designing materials with tailored spin-charge coupling.
